text:
ashok: Ran a focused sweep on fused-attn with QKV packing + bias/rope epilogue fusion. Llama-2-13B, batch=8, seq=2048, H100. Unexpected ~12% throughput drop vs baseline non-fused epilogue. Profiling attached below.

lena: Is this regression present only with KV cache enabled or also in cold path?

ashok: Only with KV cache warm path so far. Cold (no-cache) path actually gains ~6%. The cache path shows extra device->device memcpy and higher SM stall. Snippet from nvprof: 
```
Kernel: fused_attn_epilogue_qkv_pack
launch config: (1024, 4) blocks, sm_80
memcpy: 2.1 GB memcpy HtoD (unexpected), 1.8 GB DtoD
SM inst/execution: increased divergence + 18% inst_replay
```

sam: That HtoD sounds bad. Do we have a source for the memcpy? Could be layout conversion when writing back cached K/V.

ashok: Yeah looks like we pack QKV into an interleaved layout for the fused epilogue, which is great for single-pass attention, but for cached K/V we need separate contiguous K and V to avoid strided reads on subsequent tokens. We end up doing a temp buffer write+copy to convert to cached format on the warm path.

eva: Is this only on Hopper? I remember earlier A100 runs didn't show that big a hit.

ashok: Correct — A100 run had smaller regression (~3%). H100's L2 behaviour + wider warp scheduling seems to amplify the strided pattern penalty. Also observed higher DRAM BW at same kernel where A100 was compute-bound.

perf-bot: CI perf run: https://ci.redwood/prof/1801234567 (flamegraph + timeline).

sam: Workaround idea: kernel-chooser fallback: if cache_enabled && seq_len>1024 && batch>=4 then use non-fused-epilogue kernel that emits contiguous K/V writes. Quick heuristic: 
```json
{"epilogue_policy": [{"when": "cache_enabled && seq_len>1024 && batch>=4", "kernel": "epilogue_nv_nonfused"}, {"default": "epilogue_fused_qkv"}]}
```

lena: That seems reasonable as a short-term mitigation. But we should aim for a fused path that writes contiguous K and still keeps epilogue fusions for bias/rope. Maybe split packing: fused math for Q computations but produce separate K/V buffers for cache.

jonathan: I'll prototype a hybrid: do fused attention compute but have the epilogue write out separate K and V in a single kernel (avoid temp D->D memcpy). That requires reworking the write indices but should be possible. If we can write K/V in coalesced stores directly we avoid the converter step.

ashok: SGTM. Priorities: 1) Add heuristic kernel-chooser fallback to stop regression in canary (sam), 2) jonathan prototype hybrid write path, 3) run microbench harness across A100/H100 and seq 512/1024/2048 with batch sweep (ashok). Tagging @jonathan @lena @sam.

eva: Also add perf counters for L2 miss rate and device memcpy bytes so we can detect this automatically in perf alerts.

ashok: Will do. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
